title: A change to a core type rebuilds every test that uses it
goal: After a stored field was added to the middle of a core data type, a render test kept running old compiled code and failed on correct code, 3 runs out of 3, until its file was touched. A runner who sees that red suite spends a whole cycle chasing a bug that is not there, as happened on 2026-09-25. The test run should never report a failure that only a stale build causes.
notes: Reproduced 2026-10-02 in task a-menu-that-says-custom-lets-you-get-back-to-cus: added `ownPivot: MotionPivot?` and `ownCurve: EasingCurve?` to LayerMotion just above `isOn`, then `Scripts/test.sh --filter MotionRenderTests` failed 3/3: `aSwitchedOffMotionDrawsTheLayerAsItWasDrawn() ... motions: [LayerMotion(... ownPivot: nil, ownCurve: nil, isOn: true)]` after the test sets `document.layers[0].motions?[0].isOn = false`, and `difference 0.007775`. HEAD with the change stashed passed. `touch Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/MotionRenderTests.swift` then the same filter: `✔ Test run with 15 tests in 4 suites passed`. So the test object was not recompiled after the layout of a non-resilient struct changed (likely swift-driver cross-module incremental build skipping files whose used decls fingerprint the same). Same symptom and number as task a-switched-off-motion-test-passes-whichever-rend on 2026-09-25, closed as machine state. Possible fixes: build tests with -disable-incremental-imports / -enable-incremental-file-hashing flags, or have test.sh compare PhotonzCore .swiftmodule hashes and clean the test targets when they change.
acceptance: Adding a stored field ahead of an existing one in a PhotonzCore struct and running Scripts/test.sh --filter on a test target that writes that field passes without touching any test file
Or, if the build tool cannot be made to do that, Scripts/test.sh notices the stale build and rebuilds the affected target by itself, saying so in one plain line
